simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.1: One statement per line: a block, then one or more positions. # starts a comment.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.2: Position: x,y,z (x = east, y = up, z = south), each 0..255.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.3: Range: a..b on any axis, both ends included. stone 0..4,0,0..4 is a 5x1x5 plate.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.4: Corner form: stone 1,1,1..1,1,5 fills from one corner to the other.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.5: Properties: oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top] 0,3,0 - properties left out keep their default.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.6: Repeat: oak_fence 0,1,0*5@2,0,0 places 5 copies, each 2 blocks further along x.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.7: air clears what earlier lines placed: air 1..3,1..3,1..3 hollows out a box.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.8: Alias: $roof = oak_stairs[facing=north], then use it as $roof 0..4,4,0.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.9: Later lines overwrite earlier ones. minecraft: may be left out; blocks of other mods need their prefix.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.10: The Blocks tab and the search below the code show every block's ID: select one, then press Insert.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.11: Shapes instead of positions: sphere(8,8,8,5) (center, radius), dome(8,0,8,5), cylinder(4,0,4,3,6) and pyramid(4,0,4,3,4) (base center, radius, height), box(0,0,0,5,4,5) (corner, size), line(0,0,0..9,4,2). Given a box instead, e.g. sphere(0..9,0..5,0..9), they fill the same figure as an octant.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.12: hollow_ in front keeps only the shell: hollow_sphere(8,8,8,5), hollow_box(0,0,0,5,4,5). Shapes repeat like positions: stone sphere(2,2,2,1)*3@5,0,0.
simplebuilding.blueprint.help.guide.13: Variables: $r = 5, then $r works in positions, sizes and repeat counts, with + - * / % and brackets: $h = $r * 2 + 1, stone 0..$r,0,$h-1. In a position write multiplication in brackets, ($r*2), because * starts a repetition.

jei.simplebuilding.info.elytra_pad: Hands a Spawn Elytra to players with an empty chest slot in its area and recharges it. Area per tier: 1x1, 5x5, 16x16, 32x32 and 128x128 blocks (height 15 to 127); from Enderite (IV) on, boosts recharge in the whole area. Tier I is smithed from a Diamond Core (in the template slot), a diamond pressure plate and an elytra.
jei.simplebuilding.info.flypad: Grants creative flight inside its area and takes it back outside. Three enderite tiers: 4x4x8, 8x8x16 and 16x16x32 blocks; leaving the area while flying gives 10 s of Slow Falling. Tier I is crafted (shapeless) from an Enderite Core, an Enderite Pressure Plate, a Shulker Head and an elytra enchanted with Mending - a plain elytra does not fit.
jei.simplebuilding.info.spawn_teleporter: Stand still on it to travel home: to your own respawn point (bed or respawn anchor, no charge used), or to the spawn target (set by operators, otherwise the world spawn) if you have none. With a redstone signal it always takes you to the spawn target / world spawn instead - it sparkles white instead of purple and sounds like a bell and a beacon instead of a respawn anchor. Waiting time: 50 s on tier I, 20 s on Netherite II, 5 s on Enderite III. Tier I is smithed from a Gold Core (in the template slot), a light weighted pressure plate and an Enderman Head. The sound builds up over the waiting time (quarters are marked); moving cancels it. Any redstone signal strength change immediately resets the countdown, including short pulses.
jei.simplebuilding.info.chunk_loader: Keeps chunks loaded: tier I its own chunk, Netherite (II) also the four chunks sharing an edge with it (5 chunks), Enderite (III) the 3x3 chunks around it. Releases only the chunks it forced itself. Tier I is smithed from a Copper Core (in the template slot), a copper pressure plate and the head of a trial chamber mob (zombie, husk, skeleton, stray, bogged, spider, cave spider, slime, silverfish or breeze).
jei.simplebuilding.info.launchpad: Right-click with wind charges to charge it, sneak + right-click loads all charges in your hand; the higher the sound, the fuller it is. Holds 4 (I), 8 (Netherite II) or 16 (Enderite III); stand on it for 3 s to be launched. Enderite: no fall damage until the next landing. Tier I is smithed from an Iron Core (in the template slot), a heavy weighted pressure plate and the head of a trial chamber mob (zombie, husk, skeleton, stray, bogged, spider, cave spider, slime, silverfish or breeze).
jei.simplebuilding.info.potion_pad: Throw a splash or lingering potion onto the pad to store its effects (a new potion replaces the old one, a water splash potion wipes it); the potion stays in the pad until you break it. Stand on it for 3 seconds: after 1 s you have 25 %, after 2 s 50 % and after 3 s the full duration - 30 s (I), 60 s (Reinforced II) or 120 s (Infused III), but never longer than the potion itself lasts and never above the level a vanilla potion brews. Instant effects (Healing, Harming) apply once, at the 3 s mark. Beneficial effects reach everyone on the pad; harmful ones (Poison, Harming, Slowness, Levitation ...) and Glowing only the player who placed it; omens, Saturation, Absorption and other effects no potion carries are never given; mobs get nothing. The full application puts the pad on cooldown for twice the granted duration (Healing and Harming 2 min, Regeneration, Resistance and Invisibility 1.5 times, Night Vision half); Healing, Harming and Regeneration also keep that player from getting them from any pad for 60 s. Stepping off early keeps what you got and starts no cooldown. The cooldown only runs while the pad is placed: broken, it keeps the remaining time, its potion and its easter stage. Stacks to 1.
jei.simplebuilding.info.blaze_head: Dropped by a blaze killed by a charged creeper's explosion (one head per explosion, like the vanilla mob heads). Wearable and placeable; on top of a note block it plays the blaze sound. Smithed with a Netherite Core onto a Netherite Pressure Plate it makes the Potion Pad. Wear it and find out what else it is good for.
jei.simplebuilding.info.enderman_head: Dropped by an enderman killed by a charged creeper's explosion (one head per explosion, like the vanilla mob heads). Wearable and placeable; on top of a note block it plays the enderman sound. Smithed with a Gold Core onto a light weighted pressure plate it makes the Spawn Teleporter. Wear it and find out what else it is good for.
jei.simplebuilding.info.diamond_pressure: Only players press it; mobs and items do not.
jei.simplebuilding.info.netherite_pressu: With a barrel below it, only players carrying one of the barrel's items press it.
jei.simplebuilding.info.enderite_pressur: Owner-locked: the owner always presses it; with a barrel below also players named on a renamed name tag in it or carrying one of its items.
jei.simplebuilding.info.copper_pressure_: Powers only after a player has stood on it for 1-4 s, longer the more oxidized it is, and releases just as long after the player has stepped off. An axe scrapes one stage off; honeycomb waxes it (waxed plates stop oxidizing), an axe scrapes the wax off again.
jei.simplebuilding.info.spawn_elytra: Temporary elytra from the spawn area or an Elytra Pad; flight timer, boosts with jump while gliding.
jei.simplebuilding.info.amethyst_lens: Hold right-click to show a dot where you aim, visible to nearby players; the rod tilts forward, sparks, and the crosshair makes way for the dot. Held on a block for a moment the beam melts ice and snow, lights campfires, candles and soul fire, dries wet sponges, sets flammable blocks alight and primes TNT (never nether portals); held on a creature it first scans it - it glows for 5 s - and then sets it on fire (twice as long; players only with PvP). The farther away, the longer it takes (3 s up to 5 blocks, about 20 s at 200 blocks). Every use costs charge (4 per second, a full rod lasts 160 s), even pointing into the air; an empty rod never breaks - recharge it in an anvil with amethyst shards, no levels needed (16 shards = full). With Constructor's Touch (book in an anvil) it also measures: distance, target block and height in the mod's HUD box, and it remembers the last measurement. Recipe: IIR / ICA / IIR (I = iron ingot, R = redstone, C = Iron Core, A = amethyst shard).
jei.simplebuilding.info.echo_sounder: Right-click a lodestone to link it (clicking the lodestone it is already linked to does nothing), then hold use for 3 seconds to teleport onto it - no ender pearl needed. Use it deliberately: linking and every attempt that does not jump (released early, lodestone missing or jump blocked) lock it for 1 to 5 seconds depending on how far the lodestone is, shown as the item cooldown; 24 s cooldown after a jump. One jump empties the echo sounder: recharge all 1500 points with Mending XP or echo shards at an anvil before it works normally again. Used while not fully recharged it charges for 6 seconds with warning signs and shatters after the jump. Recipe: NNN / NRN / ENN (N = enderite nugget, R = recovery compass, E = enderite core).
jei.simplebuilding.info.astralit_ore: Generates in end stone near the top of the End islands; needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Astralit Dust (Silk Touch: the ore itself).
jei.simplebuilding.info.nihilith_ore: Generates in end stone on the underside of the End islands; needs a diamond pickaxe. Drops Nihilit Shards (Silk Touch: the ore itself).
jei.simplebuilding.info.sage_ore: Generates in the Overworld as rarely as diamond ore; needs an iron pickaxe. Drops 3 to 7 experience and rarely a Sage Orb (Silk Touch: the ore itself).
jei.simplebuilding.info.sage_orb: Rare drop of Sage Ore (2 %, up to 5 % with Fortune). Right-click to charge it for 0.3 seconds; it gives 50 to 100 experience.
jei.simplebuilding.info.dimensional_scra: Found in every dimension, rarer than ancient debris. Only an Enderite Pickaxe or Sledgehammer can mine it. No use yet.
jei.simplebuilding.info.astralit_dust: Mined from Astralit Ore or found in End City chests. Armor trim material and an ingredient of Ender Quartz.
jei.simplebuilding.info.nihilith_shard: Mined from Nihilit Ore or found in End City chests. Armor trim material and an ingredient of Ender Quartz.
jei.simplebuilding.info.enchanted_nether: Loot only: Ancient City chests, Bastion treasure chests and Trial Chamber vaults. Gives Regeneration II, Resistance, Fire Resistance, Absorption IV and Strength II.
jei.simplebuilding.info.enchanted_enderi: Loot only: End City chests. Gives Regeneration III, Resistance II, Fire Resistance, Absorption V, Health Boost V and Night Vision.
simplebuilding.testcentre.tweaks.potion_: then stand on it for 3 s
tooltip.simplebuilding.ore_detector.plac: Sneak + Use on a block places it; Sneak + Use in the air switches the mode
tooltip.simplebuilding.ore_detector.damp: Rock damps the signal, dense rock more.
book.simplebuilding.guide.topics.title: Topic Books
book.simplebuilding.guide.topics.text: Click a locked tab to unlock its topic.
gui.simplebuilding.guide.locked: Not in your inventory. Craft it: Book + %s
gui.simplebuilding.trim_stats.title: Resonance: %sx of max %sx
gui.simplebuilding.trim_stats.survival_h: The better of distance and time counts
gui.simplebuilding.trim_stats.cap: Cap: %sx once L, S and C are all at max
gui.simplebuilding.trim_stats.death: Dying resets L, S and C.
book.simplebuilding.guide.title: Mega Guide
book.simplebuilding.guide.1.title: Welcome
book.simplebuilding.guide.1.text:
SimpleBuilding adds tools for building, mining and storage.
Open a locked topic tab and confirm with its required item in your inventory.
book.simplebuilding.guide.2.title: Stone Chisel
book.simplebuilding.guide.2.text:
Your first tool. Right-click stone and it becomes chiseled stone bricks; sneaking turns it back.
Each change costs 1 durability, going back costs 2. Better chisels know more blocks.
book.simplebuilding.guide.3.title: Sledgehammer
book.simplebuilding.guide.3.text:
A stone hammer mines a 3x3 area; sneaking mines one block.
First block: 1.5x pickaxe time. Blocks 2-9: +0.8x each. Block 10 onward: +0.7x each.
book.simplebuilding.guide.4.title: Reshaping
book.simplebuilding.guide.4.text:
Hold right-click: block, stairs, slab.
26.3: sneak without Touch to cut the aimed corner 1.5x faster: inner corner, straight, outer corner, slab.
book.simplebuilding.guide.5.title: Diamond Pebbles
book.simplebuilding.guide.5.text:
Hold right-click with an iron hammer or better on a diamond block: 81 Diamond Pebbles.
Nine pebbles make a Cracked Diamond for Reinforced machines and chests.
book.simplebuilding.guide.6.title: Hammer Upgrades
book.simplebuilding.guide.6.text:
Hammer in hand, upgrade material in your off hand: hold right-click on a machine for 5 seconds.
Works on chests, hoppers, furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces and pistons.
book.simplebuilding.guide.7.title: Upgrade Steps
book.simplebuilding.guide.7.text:
- Cracked Diamond: copper chest
- Netherite Nugget: Reinforced
- Enderite Nugget: Netherite
Netherite needs a diamond hammer or better, Enderite a netherite one.
book.simplebuilding.guide.8.title: Building Wand
book.simplebuilding.guide.8.text:
Blocks in your off hand or hotbar, right-click a face: a whole 3x3 layer appears. A ghost preview shows where.
Sneak and right-click into the air to undo the last build.
book.simplebuilding.guide.9.title: Octant
book.simplebuilding.guide.9.text:
Measures and plans: right-click a block for Pos 1, sneak and right-click for Pos 2. The HUD shows length, area or volume.
Sneak and right-click into the air clears both. %1$s picks the shape.
book.simplebuilding.guide.10.title: Backpack
book.simplebuilding.guide.10.text:
Right-click to wear it, or just carry it. Press %2$s to open it.
Sneak and right-click a block to set it down with everything inside.
book.simplebuilding.guide.11.title: Better Tools
book.simplebuilding.guide.11.text:
Basic Upgrade at the smithing table: copper to iron to gold to diamond. Enchantments stay.
Then Netherite and Enderite. Stone chisel and hammer are starters: craft copper ones next.
book.simplebuilding.guide.12.title: Enchantments
book.simplebuilding.guide.12.text:
The enchanting table offers Fast Chiseling and Kinetic Protection. The other mod enchantments come as books from librarians, traders and chests.
Constructor's Touch unlocks the tool menu (%1$s).
book.simplebuilding.guide.13.title: Resonance
book.simplebuilding.guide.13.text:
Armor trims give real bonuses. How strong they are is your resonance - the value next to your inventory, e.g. 0.22x.
Hover over it for the details; the Trims guide explains it step by step.
book.simplebuilding.guide.14.title: Vanilla Guides
book.simplebuilding.guide.14.text:
Craft the Minecraft Mega Guide from a book and a wooden pickaxe.
Each guide has its own shelf. Unlock topics by clicking their tabs and confirming.
book.simplebuilding.tools.title: Tools & Upgrades
book.simplebuilding.tools.intro: Chisels, hammers, mining enchantments and upgrades.
book.simplebuilding.tools.1.title: Chisel Tiers
book.simplebuilding.tools.1.text: Higher tiers know more blocks: stone and sandstone; stone bricks, planks (copper, iron); quartz, deepslate (gold, diamond); Nether blocks (netherite); End palettes (enderite).
book.simplebuilding.tools.2.title: Chisel Cooldown
book.simplebuilding.tools.2.text:
After each use the chisel rests a moment, stone the longest, netherite and enderite the shortest.
Fast Chiseling cuts the rest by 30% or 60%. Constructor's Touch adds more conversions.
book.simplebuilding.tools.3.title: Hammer Speed
book.simplebuilding.tools.3.text:
Same-tier pickaxe time: first block 1.5x; blocks 2-9 add 0.8x each; from block 10 add 0.7x each.
Octant mining takes 2x per block.
book.simplebuilding.tools.4.title: Hammer Enchants
book.simplebuilding.tools.4.text:
- Radius: 3x3 becomes 5x5
- Break Through: 1 or 2 layers deeper
- Override I: every pickaxe block, not just the same kind
- Override II: everything breakable
book.simplebuilding.tools.5.title: Hammer + Octant
book.simplebuilding.tools.5.text:
Octant with both corners in your off hand: mine inside its shape to break the selection, up to 32 blocks per edge and 4096 positions.
Each block takes 2x same-tier pickaxe time and costs durability.
book.simplebuilding.tools.6.title: Upgrade Costs
book.simplebuilding.tools.6.text:
The Basic Upgrade costs twice the crafting material: pickaxe or axe 6, sword or hoe 4, shovel or chisel 2, sledgehammer 22.
A wand takes one core of the new tier. Templates hide in dungeon chests.
book.simplebuilding.tools.7.title: Vein & Strip Miner
book.simplebuilding.tools.7.text:
Both work while you sneak.
- Vein Miner: up to 3, 6, 9, 12 or 18 blocks of one ore vein with a pickaxe, or of one tree with an axe
- Strip Miner: digs 1, 2 or 4 blocks deeper
book.simplebuilding.tools.8.title: Versatility
book.simplebuilding.tools.8.text:
Versatility: sneak and left-click, and the tool swaps to the best one for the block.
Level I searches your hotbar, level II your whole inventory.
book.simplebuilding.tools.9.title: Range
book.simplebuilding.tools.9.text: Range lets chisels, mining tools, sledgehammers and octants reach farther: 2 more blocks at level I, 6 at II and 10 at III.
book.simplebuilding.tools.10.title: Armor Enchants
book.simplebuilding.tools.10.text:
Air Jump on boots: press jump again in mid-air for one more jump. Then it rests 20 seconds (10 at level II).
Kinetic Protection softens hitting a wall while flying.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.title: Enchantments
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.intro: Every mod enchantment, one tool per page: effect, top level, source.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.1.title: Fast Chiseling
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.1.text:
Max level: II. The chisel rests 30% shorter after each use, 60% at II, and mines a little faster.
From the enchanting table, librarians, toolsmiths and chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.2.title: Touch: Chisels
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.2.text:
Constructor's Touch, max level: I. A chisel learns a second set of blocks, e.g. mud, mossy cobblestone and stripped logs.
Found only in chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.3.title: Touch: Hammers
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.3.text: Constructor's Touch, max level: I. Sneak and hold right-click to reshape backwards: slab to stairs to block.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.4.title: Touch: Wands
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.4.text: Constructor's Touch, max level: I. %1$s opens the wand menu: set the radius and the axis (face, X, Y or Z).
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.5.title: Touch: Octants
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.5.text: Constructor's Touch, max level: I. The Octant shows its selection as a filled preview, so you see exactly which blocks it covers.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.6.title: Touch: Storage
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.6.text:
Constructor's Touch, max level: I.
- Quiver: feeds your bow from anywhere in your inventory
- Worn backpack: refills your hand when a block stack runs out
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.7.title: Touch: Gadgets
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.7.text:
Constructor's Touch, max level: I.
- Attractor: item filter
- Detector: half the signal loss
- Rod: measures distance
- Gauge: top and average speed
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.8.title: Touch: Stick
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.8.text: Constructor's Touch, max level: I. An enchanted stick turns blocks: right-click cycles the first orientation of the block, e.g. which way stairs face.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.9.title: Range
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.9.text:
Max level: III. Chisels, mining tools, sledgehammers and octants reach farther: 2 more blocks at I, 6 at II, 10 at III.
From librarians, toolsmiths and chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.10.text:
Max level: II. Bundles and quivers hold twice as much, four times at II.
Only from chests and fishing.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.11.text: Deep Pockets, max level: II. Each backpack slot holds twice as many items, four times at II.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.12.text:
Max level: VIII. Bundles and quivers get more room, up to three times at VIII, but only for the one kind of item already inside.
Not with Master Builder or Color Palette.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.13.text: Max level: II. Picked-up items go straight into the bundle or quiver: at I only kinds already inside, at II everything.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.14.text: Funnel, max level: II. Like on bundles, but only while you wear the backpack.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.15.text: Max level: I. The wand also takes blocks from your whole inventory, from bundles and from a worn backpack that has Master Builder too.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.16.text: Master Builder, max level: I. Right-click a block with the bundle to place the selected block from it. The wand may draw from it, too.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.17.text: Master Builder, max level: I. On a worn backpack: the wand takes blocks from it, and your bow takes arrows from quivers inside it.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.18.text:
Color Palette, max level: I. The wand mixes the blocks you carry at random - great for natural walls.
It needs Master Builder on the item first.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.19.text: Color Palette, max level: I. Placing from a Master Builder bundle picks a random block inside instead of the selected one.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.20.text:
Max level: I. The hammer mines 5x5 instead of 3x3.
Sold by the wandering trader, found in ancient cities.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.21.text: Radius, max level: I. The %3$s gets a stronger signal and searches farther.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.22.text:
Max level: II. The hammer also mines 1 layer behind the face, 2 at level II.
From toolsmiths and chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.23.text: Max level: II. At I the hammer takes every block a pickaxe mines, not just the kind you hit. At II, everything breakable.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.24.text: Max level: III. While you sneak, a pickaxe digs 1, 2 or 4 blocks deeper - slower, but in one go. Not with Vein Miner.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.25.text:
Max level: V. Sneak and mine an ore: the pickaxe takes up to 3, 6, 9, 12 or 18 blocks of the same vein.
From librarians, toolsmiths and chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.26.text: Vein Miner, max level: V. Sneak and chop a log: the axe takes the tree log by log, as many as the level allows.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.27.text:
Max level: II. Sneak and left-click: you switch to the best tool for the block, from your hotbar at I or your whole inventory at II.
Only from chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.28.text: Max level: I. The wand builds one straight line, twice as long as its area is wide, instead of a layer.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.29.text:
Max level: I. At an edge, right-click into the air: the wand builds straight ahead, 6 to 26 blocks by tier, up to the first solid block.
Only from chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.30.text:
Max level: I. Only faces of the block type you clicked get a layer. Not with Bridge or Linear.
Only from chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.31.text:
Max level: II. Press jump again in mid-air for one more jump. Then it rests 20 seconds, 10 at II; each jump costs the boots durability.
Only from chests.
book.simplebuilding.enchantments.32.text:
Max level: IV. Armor softens hitting a wall while flying. Not with the other protections.
Only from the enchanting table.
book.simplebuilding.building.title: Building
book.simplebuilding.building.1.title: Wand Tiers
book.simplebuilding.building.1.text:
- Copper 3x3, iron 5x5
- Gold 7x7, diamond 9x9
- Netherite 11x11, enderite 13x13
Each block costs one item and 1 durability. The wand builds ring by ring around the block you click.
book.simplebuilding.building.2.title: Where Blocks Come From
book.simplebuilding.building.2.text:
First your off hand, then your hotbar.
With Master Builder on the wand it also takes blocks from your whole inventory and from bundles, and from a worn backpack that has Master Builder too.
book.simplebuilding.building.3.title: Wand Menu
book.simplebuilding.building.3.text:
A wand with Constructor's Touch opens its menu with %1$s.
There you set the radius (smaller than the tier allows, if you like) and the axis: face, X, Y or Z.
book.simplebuilding.building.4.title: Undo & Hunger
book.simplebuilding.building.4.text:
Sneak and right-click into the air: the last build comes back into your inventory. Only one step, and not after you log out.
Only very large builds make you hungry; normal wand clicks are free.
book.simplebuilding.building.5.title: Linear & Bridge
book.simplebuilding.building.5.text:
Linear: the wand builds one straight line instead of a layer.
Bridge: stand at an edge and right-click into the air. The wand builds straight ahead, 6 to 26 blocks by tier, and stops at the first solid block.
book.simplebuilding.building.6.title: Cover & Color Palette
book.simplebuilding.building.6.text:
Cover: only faces of the block type you clicked get a layer. It goes with neither Bridge nor Linear.
Color Palette mixes the blocks you carry at random - great for natural walls.
book.simplebuilding.building.7.title: Octant Shapes
book.simplebuilding.building.7.text:
%1$s opens the Octant menu: cuboid, cylinder, prism, pyramid, sphere, rectangle or ellipse, plus orientation and hollow.
Dye it to tell several apart.
book.simplebuilding.building.8.title: Octant + Wand
book.simplebuilding.building.8.text:
An Octant with both corners in your off hand, a wand in your main hand: the wand fills the shape.
Example: a prism pointing up, with stairs first on your hotbar, becomes a roof.
book.simplebuilding.building.9.title: Blueprint
book.simplebuilding.building.9.text:
Right-click to open the editor. Write a build code or insert an example, then sign it.
To build: Blueprint in your off hand, wand in your main hand, click.
book.simplebuilding.building.10.title: Build Code
book.simplebuilding.building.10.text:
One line per part: block, then x,y,z. Ranges are written a..b.
Example: oak_planks 0..4,0,0..4 lays a 5x5 floor. The book button in the editor opens a guide and a block list.
book.simplebuilding.building.11.title: Scanning
book.simplebuilding.building.11.text:
In a cartography table: an Octant with both corners on top, an empty Blueprint below.
The Blueprint copies the selected building, the Octant stays. Sign the copy before you build with it.
book.simplebuilding.building.12.title: Construction Light
book.simplebuilding.building.12.text:
Shines at full brightness while you build at night.
Its light does not stop monsters from spawning, so it is no replacement for torches.
book.simplebuilding.building.13.title: Quartz Checkers
book.simplebuilding.building.13.text:
Two quartz blocks crossed with two of another material make four checker blocks.
Partners: purpur, lapis block, blackstone, red nether bricks, Astralit Dust, Nihilit Shard or Ender Quartz.
book.simplebuilding.building.14.title: Small Tricks
book.simplebuilding.building.14.text:
Right-click placed wool with shears: it turns back into 4 string.
A water cauldron washes the dye off Octants, backpacks and the mod's bundles and quivers.
book.simplebuilding.storage.title: Storage
book.simplebuilding.storage.1.title: Bundles
book.simplebuilding.storage.1.text:
The Reinforced Bundle holds 96 items, Netherite 192, Enderite 288.
Upgrading keeps everything inside, including enchantments and name.
book.simplebuilding.storage.2.title: Quivers
book.simplebuilding.storage.2.text:
Arrows only: 64, 96, 128 or 192 by tier.
Your bow and crossbow draw from it in your off hand, chest slot or hotbar; with Constructor's Touch also from the rest of your inventory.
book.simplebuilding.storage.3.title: Backpacks
book.simplebuilding.storage.3.text:
Four tiers: 9, 18, 33 and 50 slots, worn they add 1 to 4 armor points.
Press %2$s to open it, worn or anywhere in your inventory.
book.simplebuilding.storage.4.title: Wearing & Placing
book.simplebuilding.storage.4.text:
Right-click to wear it in the chest slot; it swaps with a chestplate or elytra.
Sneak and right-click a block to set it down with its contents. Backpacks do not fit into other containers.
book.simplebuilding.storage.5.title: Chests
book.simplebuilding.storage.5.text:
- Reinforced Chest: 36 slots
- Netherite Chest: 45 slots, stacks twice as big
- Enderite Chest: 54 slots, stacks four times as big
Hammer a copper chest to start (see the Beginner's Guide).
book.simplebuilding.storage.6.title: Deep Pockets & Drawer
book.simplebuilding.storage.6.text:
Deep Pockets doubles the room, level II four times.
Drawer (bundles and quivers) adds room for the one kind of item already inside. It does not go with Master Builder or Color Palette.
book.simplebuilding.storage.7.title: Funnel
book.simplebuilding.storage.7.text:
Funnel picks up items for you. Level I takes only kinds already inside, level II everything.
A backpack funnels only while you wear it.
book.simplebuilding.storage.8.title: Master Builder
book.simplebuilding.storage.8.text:
On a bundle or quiver: you can place blocks from it, and the wand may draw from it.
On a worn backpack: the wand takes blocks from it, and your bow takes quivers from it.
book.simplebuilding.machines.title: Machines & Pistons
book.simplebuilding.machines.intro: Faster hoppers and furnaces, stronger pistons and sand that ignores gravity.
book.simplebuilding.machines.1.title: Hoppers
book.simplebuilding.machines.1.text:
A vanilla hopper moves one item every 8 ticks. Reinforced takes 4, Netherite 2, Enderite 1.
Netherite and Enderite hoppers are hammered in the world, not crafted.
book.simplebuilding.machines.2.title: Hopper Filters
book.simplebuilding.machines.2.text:
Each slot has a filter item. The button cycles Disabled, Exact Match (item and data) and Type Match (item only).
With the filter on, a slot without a filter item accepts nothing.
book.simplebuilding.machines.3.title: Furnaces
book.simplebuilding.machines.3.text:
Reinforced furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces run 2x as fast, Netherite 4x, Enderite 8x, and the extra speed burns no extra fuel.
Netherite and Enderite give double experience.
book.simplebuilding.machines.4.title: Bonus Ingots
book.simplebuilding.machines.4.text:
Raw iron, gold and copper in upgraded blast furnaces:
- Netherite: one extra ingot every 4th smelt
- Enderite: one extra every 2nd
book.simplebuilding.machines.5.title: Reinforced Piston
book.simplebuilding.machines.5.text:
Pushes 18 blocks instead of 12.
With a redstone block behind it or at its side, it pushes one unbreakable block such as bedrock. The redstone block is used up.
book.simplebuilding.machines.6.title: Breaker Pistons
book.simplebuilding.machines.6.text:
Netherite and Enderite pistons break the block in front instead of pushing it; it drops as an item.
The stronger the signal, the harder the block: weak breaks dirt, 15 nearly anything.
book.simplebuilding.machines.7.title: Breaker Wear
book.simplebuilding.machines.7.text:
Each broken block costs the breaker piston one use. Right-click it with its nugget to repair it fully.
Worn out, it drops one tier. Servers can turn wear off.
book.simplebuilding.machines.8.title: Gravity Blocks
book.simplebuilding.machines.8.text:
Suspended sand and gravel stay in the air where you place them.
Levitating sand and gravel rise up on their own until a ceiling stops them.
book.simplebuilding.end.title: End & Enderite
book.simplebuilding.end.intro: New ores, the Enderite tier and three End palettes.
book.simplebuilding.end.1.title: End Ores
book.simplebuilding.end.1.text:
Astralit Ore glows on top of the End islands, Nihilit Ore hides on their undersides.
Both need a diamond pickaxe; Fortune gives more dust and shards.
book.simplebuilding.end.2.title: Enderite Loot
book.simplebuilding.end.2.text:
End city chests hold the Enderite materials: raw ore, nuggets, scrap and the Enderite upgrade template.
Raw Enderite can also be crafted from Nihilit, Astralit and an ender pearl.
book.simplebuilding.end.3.title: Refining
book.simplebuilding.end.3.text:
Three Raw Enderite stacked in a column make %3$s. A blast furnace turns it into scrap in two hours - faster in upgraded ones.
Scrap, diamonds and a netherite ingot make the ingot.
book.simplebuilding.end.4.title: Enderite Gear
book.simplebuilding.end.4.text:
At the smithing table: Enderite Upgrade, a netherite item and an Enderite Ingot. Enchantments stay.
Enderite gear does not burn and lasts longer than netherite.
book.simplebuilding.end.5.title: Void Safe
book.simplebuilding.end.5.text:
Dropped Enderite items do not fall out of the world: below the bottom they float in place.
Enderite armor slows void damage, and with two or more pieces you drift down while you hold jump.
book.simplebuilding.end.6.title: End Palettes
book.simplebuilding.end.6.text:
Pink Astralit, blue Nihilit and purple Ender Quartz: polished blocks, bricks, stairs, slabs, walls, pillars and chiseled blocks.
Every Astralit block glows.
book.simplebuilding.end.7.title: Enderite Food
book.simplebuilding.end.7.text:
The Enderite Apple heals, shields you and adds hearts for two minutes.
The Enderite Carrot gives night vision for five minutes, plus speed and jump boost for one.
book.simplebuilding.end.8.title: Enderite Spear
book.simplebuilding.end.8.text:
Smith a netherite spear with the Enderite Upgrade and an Enderite Ingot.
Like all Enderite gear it does not burn and does not fall out of the world.
book.simplebuilding.pads.title: Pads
book.simplebuilding.pads.intro: Plates and pads to fly, launch, teleport, share potions and load chunks.
book.simplebuilding.pads.1.title: Pressure Plates
book.simplebuilding.pads.1.text:
- Diamond: reacts to players only
- Copper: waits 1 to 4 seconds, longer the more it has oxidized
- Netherite, Enderite: filter plates (next page)
book.simplebuilding.pads.2.title: Filter Plates
book.simplebuilding.pads.2.text:
Put a barrel below. A Netherite plate then opens only for players carrying one of the barrel's items.
An Enderite plate always opens for its owner, and for players named on renamed name tags in the barrel.
book.simplebuilding.pads.3.title: Waxing Plates
book.simplebuilding.pads.3.text:
Copper plates oxidize like copper blocks, and the more oxidized, the longer they wait.
Honeycomb waxes them so they stay as they are; an axe scrapes off the wax or one stage.
book.simplebuilding.pads.4.title: Owners & Redstone
book.simplebuilding.pads.4.text:
Pads belong to whoever placed them; strangers need a minute to break one.
Redstone disables flight and launch pads; teleporters instead use world spawn. Comparators read pads out.
book.simplebuilding.pads.5.title: Elytra Pads
book.simplebuilding.pads.5.text:
Step inside its area with an empty chest slot: you get a Spawn Elytra with a few rocket boosts.
It cannot be stored, and it disappears after five minutes or when you land outside a pad area.
book.simplebuilding.pads.6.title: Launchpads
book.simplebuilding.pads.6.text:
Load it with wind charges by hand or with a hopper. Stand on it for 3 seconds and it launches you - the more charges, the higher.
The top tier also saves you from fall damage.
book.simplebuilding.pads.7.title: Flypads
book.simplebuilding.pads.7.text:
Inside its area you can fly like in creative mode, and you glow for everyone to see.
Near the edge a sound warns you; outside you get Slow Falling for 10 seconds.
book.simplebuilding.pads.8.title: Spawn Teleporter
book.simplebuilding.pads.8.text:
Stand still: after 50, 20 or 5 seconds by tier, you reach your bed or anchor, otherwise the spawn target.
Redstone selects the spawn target. Moving or any signal strength change resets the timer.
book.simplebuilding.pads.9.title: Potion Pads
book.simplebuilding.pads.9.text:
Throw a splash or lingering potion onto it. Players who stand on it for 3 seconds get its effect for 30, 60 or 120 seconds by tier.
Harmful effects reach only the owner.
book.simplebuilding.pads.10.title: Chunk Loaders
book.simplebuilding.pads.10.text:
Keeps chunks loaded so farms keep running: tier I its own chunk, II also the four next to it, III a 3x3 area.
By default it only works while its owner is online.
book.simplebuilding.pads.11.title: Mob Heads
book.simplebuilding.pads.11.text:
Charged creepers drop heads from blazes, endermen, shulkers and trial chamber mobs.
Heads unlock pads, play mob sounds on note blocks and hide small abilities when worn.
book.simplebuilding.pads.12.title: Pad Upgrades
book.simplebuilding.pads.12.text:
Tier I uses a material core. The recipe cards show each pad.
Flypad I is crafted with an Enderite Core, plate, Shulker Head and Mending elytra. Higher tiers use the smithing table.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.title: Gadgets
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.intro: Handy tools that pull, turn, find, jump and measure.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.1.title: Attractor
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.1.text:
Hold the %3$s: items within 3 blocks fly to you. Range adds 1.5 per level, up to 7.5. Sneaking pauses it.
With Constructor's Touch, sneak-click a block or item to filter.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.2.title: Placed Attractor
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.2.text:
Place it: sneak-click without Constructor's Touch, right-click with it. Default range: 6 blocks; a hopper below collects items.
Held or placed: dead zone 1.25 blocks by default.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.3.title: Rotator
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.3.text:
Turns logs, furnaces, pistons, hoppers, stairs and signs in place. Click near an edge of a face to choose the direction; sneaking turns backwards.
Extended pistons stay as they are.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.4.title: Rotator Charge
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.4.text:
Each turn costs one of 1024 charges; Unbreaking saves some. An empty Rotator never breaks.
At an anvil, 16 ender pearls fill it again - no levels needed. Mending does not work on it.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.5.title: Finding Ores
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.5.text:
The %3$s points to the nearest ore of its mode: iron, gold, diamond, netherite, all, or a custom block.
Sneak and use to change the mode; sneak-click a block to make it the custom target.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.6.title: Signal Strength
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.6.text:
Rock between you and the ore weakens the signal: air barely, stone more, deepslate and obsidian a lot.
Radius extends the search, Constructor's Touch halves the loss.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.7.title: Echo Sounder
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.7.text:
Right-click a lodestone to link it. Hold use for 3 seconds to jump; releasing early cancels.
After a jump: 24 seconds cooldown. Linking and failed attempts: 1 to 5 seconds by distance.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.8.title: Echo Charge
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.8.text:
A jump empties the echo sounder. Four echo shards at an anvil or Mending refill it.
Used before it is full, it still jumps after a short charge-up - and then shatters.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.9.title: Resonance Rod
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.9.text:
Hold right-click for a red dot. Kept on one spot, the beam melts ice and snow, lights campfires and candles, dries sponges and primes TNT.
Far away it takes longer.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.10.title: Rod Charge
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.10.text:
Pointing costs 4 charges per second by default. An empty rod never breaks.
Recharge at an anvil with amethyst shards, no levels needed: 16 shards fill it.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.11.title: Gauge
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.11.text:
Hold it: the dial shows speed. In the air it adds height above ground and estimated fall damage.
Constructor's Touch adds top and average speed. Range measures deeper.
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.12.title: Netherite Food
book.simplebuilding.gadgets.12.text:
Netherite Apple: fire resistance, resistance, absorption and regeneration.
Netherite Carrot: fire resistance and night vision for two minutes. Neither burns in lava.
book.simplebuilding.trims.title: Trims & Radiance
book.simplebuilding.trims.intro: Trims with real bonuses, resonance and armor that shines.
book.simplebuilding.trims.1.title: Trim Bonuses
book.simplebuilding.trims.1.text:
Every trim pattern and material gives a bonus: less damage of a kind, speed, experience, luck and more.
The armor tooltip lists them. Netherite and Enderite trims count the pattern more.
book.simplebuilding.trims.2.title: Resonance
book.simplebuilding.trims.2.text:
How strong the bonuses are is your resonance: from 0.20x up to 2.00x.
The small field next to your inventory shows it, e.g. 0.22x. Hover over it to see the details.
book.simplebuilding.trims.3.title: Three Factors
book.simplebuilding.trims.3.text:
- L: experience
- S: survival
- C: combat
Each ranges from 0.10 to 1.00 (max 1.00). Resonance = their average x 2.0. All three at 1.00: the cap of 2.00x.
book.simplebuilding.trims.4.title: L: Experience
book.simplebuilding.trims.4.text:
Counts the experience points you gathered since your last death. 1395 points (level 0 to 30) fill it to 1.00.
Spending levels on enchanting or anvils costs you nothing.
book.simplebuilding.trims.5.title: S: Survival
book.simplebuilding.trims.5.text:
The better of two: distance traveled or active time. Standing still for a minute stops the clock.
Example: 4000 blocks or one hour give 0.67, 12000 blocks or three hours 0.96.
book.simplebuilding.trims.6.title: C: Combat
book.simplebuilding.trims.6.text:
Monster kills count 1 point, animals 0.2, and taking damage adds a little.
Example: 100 points give 0.67, 300 points 0.96.
book.simplebuilding.trims.7.title: Death
book.simplebuilding.trims.7.text:
Dying resets all three factors to 0.10, so your resonance drops back to 0.20x.
Staying alive is what makes trims strong.
book.simplebuilding.trims.8.title: Bonus Caps
book.simplebuilding.trims.8.text:
Bonuses have their own limits, whatever your resonance:
- at least 20% of each hit gets through
- all-damage bonuses together: 25%
- speed +20%, experience +50%, luck +3
book.simplebuilding.trims.9.title: End Materials
book.simplebuilding.trims.9.text:
Astralit trims make you jump higher, Nihilit trims pull you down faster while you sneak in the air.
Enderite trims soften almost every kind of damage and count the pattern double.
book.simplebuilding.trims.10.title: Radiance
book.simplebuilding.trims.10.text:
Hit a placed trim template three times with a sledgehammer and Glowstone Dust in your off hand: an %3$s.
Dust at the smithing table raises radiance up to 5.
book.simplebuilding.trims.11.title: Glowing
book.simplebuilding.trims.11.text:
Do the same with a Glow Ink Sac instead: a %3$s.
The trim glows at full brightness, but gives no light to the world.
book.simplebuilding.trims.12.title: Pulsating
book.simplebuilding.trims.12.text:
The %3$s makes a trim pulse. Alone its colors fade to gray and back; with Glowing its glow swells and fades.
The hammer stays in the crafting grid.
book.simplebuilding.trims.13.title: Placing Templates
book.simplebuilding.trims.13.text:
Sneak and right-click with a smithing template to lay it on the floor, a wall or the ceiling.
A placed trim template takes three sledgehammer hits to upgrade.
book.simplebuilding.trims.14.title: Trim Icons
book.simplebuilding.trims.14.text: Trimmed armor shows its pattern on the item icon in the colors of its material, so you can tell trims apart without wearing them.
Rules for those who make them.
book.simplebuilding.admin.title: Server Admin
book.simplebuilding.admin.intro: Commands and config switches. Only operators can craft this book.
book.simplebuilding.admin.1.title: Who May Use Them
book.simplebuilding.admin.1.text: The commands /simplebuilding, /killboats and /killcarts need an operator player. The console and command blocks cannot use them.
book.simplebuilding.admin.2.title: Reading Options
book.simplebuilding.admin.2.text:
/simplebuilding config list shows every option; a filter such as tweaks.pads narrows it.
/simplebuilding config get shows value, default and type.
book.simplebuilding.admin.3.title: Changing Options
book.simplebuilding.admin.3.text:
/simplebuilding config set changes an option, /simplebuilding config reset restores its default.
Both keep the limits, save the file at once and update the clients.
book.simplebuilding.admin.4.title: Pad Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.4.text:
/simplebuilding tweaks pads flypads false switches a pad type off. Potion pads are only in the config: tweaks.pads.enablePotionPads.
The same works as config set tweaks.pads.enableFlypads.
book.simplebuilding.admin.5.title: Spawn Target
book.simplebuilding.admin.5.text:
/simplebuilding tweaks worldspawn setspawn1 aims every Spawn Teleporter at the spot where you stand.
Unset, they lead to world spawn.
book.simplebuilding.admin.6.title: Chunk Loaders
book.simplebuilding.admin.6.text:
/simplebuilding chunkloaders list shows every chunk loader with owner and state; remove deletes one.
There is no limit per player. By default a loader runs only while its owner is online.
book.simplebuilding.admin.7.title: Vehicles
book.simplebuilding.admin.7.text:
/killboats and /killcarts clear empty vehicles within tweaks.commands.killCommandRadius; add empty or all for chest ones too.
/killcarts is off until tweaks.commands.enableKillCartsCommand.
book.simplebuilding.admin.8.title: World Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.8.text:
giveGuideBookOnFirstJoin: ignored on 26.3.
worldGen.enableLootTableChanges: chest loot; applies on /reload.
book.simplebuilding.admin.9.title: Trade Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.9.text: worldGen.enableVillagerTrades and worldGen.enableWanderingTrades add the mod's trades; both apply on /reload.
book.simplebuilding.admin.10.title: Gameplay Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.10.text: trimBenefitBaseMultiplier sets the resonance base (2.0), airJumpCooldownTicks the rest after an Air Jump.
book.simplebuilding.admin.11.title: Tool Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.11.text: breakerPistonsLoseDurability turns breaker piston wear on or off, tools.buildingWandHungerCost the hunger of huge wand builds.
book.simplebuilding.admin.12.title: Feature Switches
book.simplebuilding.admin.12.text: The server.features options switch features off. For backpacks, Attractors, Echo Sounders, blueprints, Detectors and levitating blocks, recipes also disappear on reload.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.title: Minecraft Guide
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.1.text:
This guide explains Minecraft 26.3, one idea per page. Recipe cards stand next to the text.
Click a locked tab and confirm with its required item in your inventory.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.2.text:
Punch a tree to get logs. One log makes four planks.
Four planks make a crafting table: place it to use the 3x3 grid. Two planks stacked make four sticks.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.3.text:
A wooden pickaxe mines stone, which drops cobblestone. Stone tools are faster and last longer.
A stone pickaxe also mines iron, copper and lapis ore.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.4.text:
Monsters spawn in darkness, at block light 0. Torches keep them away.
Before the first night, build a hut or dig into a hill and close the door behind you.
No coal? Smelt logs into charcoal.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.5.text:
You heal on your own while your hunger bar is at 18 or more (nine shanks). Below 7 you cannot sprint.
Cooked meat fills far more than raw: cooked beef gives 8 hunger points.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.6.text:
Sleeping in a bed skips the night and sets your respawn point.
New: the Straw Bed, made from hay bales. It skips the night too, but never sets your spawn and breaks when you get up.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.7.text:
A furnace turns ore, sand and food into something new. Fuel goes below, the item on top.
The smoker cooks food and the blast furnace smelts ores, both twice as fast.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.8.text:
Iron opens the game up. An iron pickaxe mines gold, diamonds, redstone and emeralds.
Make a shield and a bucket early: water puts out fire and breaks falls.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.9.text:
A chest holds 27 stacks; two side by side make a double chest with 54. A barrel holds 27 and can have a block on top.
Bundles carry many kinds of items in one slot.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.10.tex:
When you die, your items drop where you fell. Loaded, they vanish after five minutes.
A recovery compass points to the place of your last death. It needs echo shards from ancient cities.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_start.11.tex:
Villagers trade for emeralds. A job site block gives them a profession, e.g. a lectern makes a librarian, a composter a farmer.
The more you trade, the better their offers get.
tooltip.simplebuilding.guide_book.vanill: The world under the open sky.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_overworld.in: Biomes, weather and the places worth visiting above ground.
The world is split into biomes: forests, plains, deserts, jungles, swamps, snowy slopes and more.
Each has its own blocks, trees and animals, so travel pays off.
Every wood type has its own sapling; plant it on dirt or grass with room above.
Bone meal makes it grow at once. Dark oak and giant spruce need four saplings in a square.
New in 26.x: the Dappled Forest with poplar trees in yellow, orange and red leaves.
Poplar gives a full wood set. Look for red shrubs and shelf mushrooms on the trunks - they are bouncy.
Emerald ore only forms in mountain biomes, and iron is plentiful high up.
Watch out for powder snow: you sink into it and freeze. Leather boots let you walk on it.
Villages come in five styles: plains, desert, savanna, snowy and taiga. Iron golems guard them.
Ring the bell and villagers run inside. Help them against raids and they give you discounts.
- Desert pyramid: loot, but a TNT trap below
- Jungle temple: tripwire traps
- Igloo: some hide a basement
- Witch hut, pillager outpost
- Woodland mansion: rare and dangerous
New in 26.x: abandoned camps in forests, taigas, savannas and more.
The chest holds copper gear, a copper spear, a spyglass and maps. Search well: a secret chest may hold diamonds.
Brush suspicious sand and gravel at trail ruins, desert pyramids, desert wells and ocean ruins.
You find pottery sherds, trim templates and even a sniffer egg.
A full day lasts 20 minutes, the night about 7 of them.
In thunderstorms monsters spawn in daylight too. Lightning can set fires; a lightning rod catches it safely.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_overworld.10:
A compass points to the world spawn; on a lodestone it points there instead.
Maps draw the land as you walk. A cartography table zooms, copies and locks them.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.title: Caves & Underground
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.intro: Ores, cave biomes and the dangers below.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.1.text:
The Overworld reaches from Y -64 to Y 320. Press F3 to see your Y.
Below Y 0 stone turns into deepslate, which is slower to mine. At the very bottom lies unbreakable bedrock.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.2.text:
- Coal: Y 96, and all over mountains
- Copper: Y 48
- Iron: Y 16 (and high mountains)
- Lapis: Y 0
- Gold: Y -16
- Diamond, redstone: Y -58
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.3.text:
For diamonds, dig a long tunnel at Y -58 and side tunnels every three blocks: you see every block in between.
Fortune gives more diamonds, coal, redstone and lapis per ore.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.4.text:
- Lush caves: moss, glow berries, axolotls
- Dripstone caves: pointed dripstone, large copper veins
- Deep dark: sculk and the warden
- Sulfur caves: new, see next page
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.5.text:
New in 26.x: sulfur caves with sulfur spikes, sulfur pools and bands of red cinnabar in the stone.
Potent sulfur is a geyser: over lava it erupts all the time, over a magma block now and then.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.6.text:
Sulfur cubes live only in sulfur caves. They swallow a block, and that block changes how they move.
Wood makes them bouncy, ice fast, TNT explosive. Slime balls breed them; a bucket carries them.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.7.text:
Sculk sensors hear footsteps; shriekers answer. After three shrieks the warden rises.
It is blind but hears and smells you. Sneak, never fight it. Ancient cities hold echo shards and Swift Sneak books.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.8.text:
Mineshafts hold chest minecarts and cave spider spawners. Dungeons are small rooms with a spawner and chests.
New: mineshafts can hold the disc Bounce, and name tags are craftable now.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.9.text:
Copper halls full of trial spawners. Beat a wave to earn a trial key, then open a vault with it.
Breezes drop breeze rods. A heavy core from an ominous vault and a breeze rod make the mace.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_caves.10.tex:
Deep caves hold lava lakes. Never dig straight down.
Carry a water bucket, spare blocks, torches and food. Place torches on one side only - then you always find the way back.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.title: The Ocean
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.1.text:
Boats are the fastest way across water, and they seat two. A chest boat carries 27 stacks instead of a passenger.
Bamboo makes a raft.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.2.text:
Underwater your air lasts 15 seconds. Respiration adds time, Aqua Affinity mines at full speed.
A turtle shell gives 10 seconds of water breathing each time you dive.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.3.text:
Warm oceans grow coral reefs, frozen ones carry icebergs. Deep oceans hide monuments.
Coral dies outside water - mine it with Silk Touch. Dried kelp is a quick snack.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.4.text:
Shipwrecks hold chests with loot and buried treasure maps.
Follow the map to the X and dig: the buried chest holds a heart of the sea. New: ocean ruins give such maps too.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.5.text:
Guardians shoot lasers; three elder guardians give you Mining Fatigue.
Inside: sponges, eight gold blocks and the Tide template. Bring milk, Night Vision and Water Breathing.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.6.text:
A heart of the sea and eight nautilus shells make a conduit. Frame it with prismarine under water.
It gives breathing, night vision and faster mining nearby; a full frame attacks monsters.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.7.text:
Drowned are zombies of the sea. Some carry a trident - the only way to get one besides trial vaults.
Loyalty brings it back, Riptide pulls you along in rain, Channeling calls lightning.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.8.text:
Nautiluses swim in the oceans and can carry you through the water.
Fish breeds them, and nautilus armor from copper to netherite protects them. Beware of zombie nautiluses.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.9.text:
Cast into open water and pull when the bobber dips. Besides fish you catch junk and treasure: enchanted books, saddles, name tags.
Luck of the Sea finds more treasure, Lure bites sooner.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_ocean.10.tex:
Axolotls from lush caves fight drowned and guardians at your side. A bucket of tropical fish breeds them.
Turtles return to their home beach to lay eggs; the babies shed scutes.
tooltip.simplebuilding.guide_book.vanill: Hot, loud and full of gold.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.title: The Nether
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.1.tex:
Build an obsidian frame at least 4 wide and 5 tall; the corners may stay empty. Light it with flint and steel.
No diamond pickaxe yet? Pour water over lava to cast obsidian.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.2.tex:
One block in the Nether is eight in the Overworld. Build a portal at your X and Z divided by 8 and it links to your base.
That makes the Nether a fast road.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.3.tex:
Water boils away and beds explode. A lava ocean lies at Y 31.
Ghasts shoot fireballs - hit them back. A fire resistance potion is the best life insurance.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.4.tex:
- Nether wastes: the classic
- Crimson forest: hoglins, piglins
- Warped forest: endermen, calm
- Soul sand valley: skeletons, ghasts
- Basalt deltas: magma cubes
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.5.tex:
Wear one piece of gold armor and piglins leave you alone. Toss them gold ingots to barter.
They give obsidian, ender pearls, fire resistance potions, Soul Speed books and more. Never open their chests.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.6.tex:
Dark brick bridges and halls. Blazes drop blaze rods for brewing and eyes of ender.
Wither skeletons may drop skulls. Nether wart grows on the stairs; chests hold diamonds and saddles.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.7.tex:
Huge blackstone ruins full of piglins and brutes - brutes ignore gold armor.
Every chest can hold a netherite upgrade template; the treasure room hides gold blocks and ancient debris.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.8.tex:
The rarest ore, best at Y 15 in the Nether. It needs a diamond pickaxe and resists explosions - beds and TNT uncover it.
Smelt it into scrap; four scrap and four gold make an ingot.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.9.tex:
At the smithing table: upgrade template, a diamond item and a netherite ingot. Enchantments stay.
Copy the template with seven diamonds and netherrack. Netherite items do not burn in lava.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.10.te:
Saddle a strider and steer it across lava with a warped fungus on a stick.
Piglins sometimes barter a dried ghast: keep it in water and it becomes a ghastling that grows into a rideable happy ghast.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_nether.11.te:
Beds explode here, but a respawn anchor charged with glowstone sets your spawn in the Nether.
Each respawn uses one charge. In the Overworld it explodes too.
tooltip.simplebuilding.guide_book.vanill: Where the game has its credits.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.title: The End
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.intro: The stronghold, the dragon and the islands beyond.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.1.title: Eyes of Ender
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.1.text:
An ender pearl and blaze powder make an eye of ender. Thrown, it flies toward the nearest stronghold and sometimes breaks.
Follow it, throw again, and dig down where it sinks.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.2.title: The Portal
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.2.text:
Deep in the stronghold lies a portal of twelve frames. Fill every empty frame with an eye of ender to open it.
Block the silverfish spawner first. The only way back is killing the dragon.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.3.title: Preparing
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.3.text:
- Blocks to build up and bridge
- A bow and many arrows
- A carved pumpkin: endermen ignore your gaze
- Food, and potions of slow falling
- No beds: they explode
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.4.title: The Ender Dragon
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.4.text:
End crystals on the obsidian pillars heal the dragon. Shoot them first; the caged ones need climbing.
When the dragon perches on the portal, hit it hard, but stay out of its purple breath.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.5.title: After the Fight
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.5.text:
The dragon leaves lots of experience, an exit portal home and the dragon egg on top of it.
The egg teleports when you hit it: push it off with a piston. Collect dragon's breath in bottles.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.6.title: End Gateways
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.6.text:
Each defeat of the dragon opens a small gateway at the edge of the island.
Throw an ender pearl into it to reach the outer islands, where the real treasure waits.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.7.title: End Cities
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.7.text:
Purple towers on the outer islands. Shulkers hide in the walls; their shots make you float.
Chests hold diamond gear and the Spire template. Some cities have a ship with an elytra and a dragon head.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.8.title: Elytra
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.8.text:
Wear the elytra in the chest slot, jump and press jump again in mid-air to glide.
Firework rockets boost you. It never breaks fully; repair it with phantom membranes or Mending.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.9.title: Shulker Boxes
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.9.text:
Two shulker shells and a chest make a shulker box. Broken, it keeps everything inside.
So you carry 27 stacks in one slot. Dye it to sort your boxes.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.10.title: Chorus Plants
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_end.10.text:
Chorus fruit teleports you a few blocks when eaten - handy in a pinch.
Smelted it pops, and popped chorus fruit makes purpur blocks and end rods.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.int: Signals, switches and machines that work for you.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.1.t:
Redstone dust carries a signal with strength 15 that drops by one per block.
Sources: levers stay on, buttons and pressure plates pulse, redstone torches and blocks are always on.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.2.t:
A repeater boosts a signal back to 15 and lets it pass only one way.
Right-click it for a delay of 1 to 4 ticks. Powered from the side by another repeater, it locks.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.3.t:
A comparator reads how full a chest, hopper or furnace is and outputs that as signal strength.
It compares or subtracts two signals; right-click switches the mode.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.4.t:
A redstone torch on a block turns off when that block is powered: on becomes off and off becomes on.
With this NOT gate you build every logic circuit.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.5.t:
A piston pushes up to 12 blocks; a sticky piston pulls the first one back.
Obsidian and bedrock never move. Slime and honey blocks drag their neighbors along.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.6.t:
An observer watches the block in front of its face and sends a short pulse out the back whenever it changes.
Example: an observer sees sugar cane grow and fires a piston that cuts it.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.7.t:
Hoppers pull items from above and pass them on; a redstone signal stops them.
Droppers spit items out. Dispensers use them: they shoot arrows, place water and put armor on stands.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.8.t:
The crafter crafts one item on every redstone pulse. Hoppers fill it, and clicking a slot disables it.
So the pattern stays put and the crafter builds an automatic workshop.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_redstone.9.t:
A copper bulb toggles on or off with every pulse and remembers its state - a one-block memory.
It grows dimmer as it oxidizes; honeycomb wax keeps its brightness.
- Daylight detector: sunlight, or night when inverted
- Target block: the closer to the center, the stronger
- Sculk sensor: hears vibrations
- Tripwire: a hidden line
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.title: Tools, Armor & Weapons
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.intro: Materials, enchanting, anvils and how to fight.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.1.title: Tool Tiers
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.1.text:
Wood, stone, copper, iron, gold, diamond, netherite. Better tiers mine faster and last longer.
Stone mines iron, iron mines diamond, diamond mines obsidian and ancient debris. Gold is fast but fragile.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.2.title: Armor
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.2.text:
Leather, copper, chainmail, iron, gold, diamond, netherite. The chestplate protects most.
Diamond and netherite add toughness against big hits; netherite also resists knockback.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.3.title: Swords & Axes
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.3.text:
Wait for the attack bar to refill: full hits deal full damage. A sword sweeps enemies next to the target.
An axe hits harder but slower, and it disables a shield for a moment.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.4.title: Spears
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.4.text:
Spears come in every tool material and reach farther than a sword.
Hold use to charge: the faster you move, the harder you hit - strongest from horseback. Lunge adds a dash.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.5.title: Bows & Crossbows
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.5.text:
Draw the bow fully for the strongest shot. A crossbow stays loaded until you fire and can shoot fireworks.
Crossbow enchantments: Multishot, Piercing, Quick Charge.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.6.title: The Mace
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.6.text:
A heavy core on a breeze rod. The farther you fall before the hit, the more damage - and you take no fall damage.
Density, Breach and Wind Burst improve it.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.7.title: Enchanting
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.7.text:
An enchanting table with 15 bookshelves around it, one block away, offers level 30 enchantments.
Each costs lapis and levels. Enchanting a book lets you choose its target later.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.8.title: Anvils
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.8.text:
Combine two items or add an enchanted book, repair with material, or rename.
Every use makes the next one dearer; at 40 levels it says Too Expensive. Plan the order of your books.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.9.title: Mending & Grindstone
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.9.text:
Mending repairs an item with the experience you collect while holding or wearing it.
A grindstone removes enchantments (curses stay) and returns some experience.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.10.text:
- V: Sharpness, Efficiency, Power
- IV: Protection, Feather Falling
- III: Unbreaking, Fortune, Looting
- II: Fire Aspect, Knockback
- I: Mending, Silk Touch, Infinity
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_gear.11.text:
The smithing table upgrades diamond gear to netherite and adds armor trims.
A trim needs a template, the armor and a material that sets its color. Seven diamonds copy a template.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.intr: Crops, animals, pets and the monsters of the night.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.1.te:
Till dirt with a hoe and plant seeds, carrots, potatoes or beetroot. Water up to four blocks away keeps farmland wet.
Crops need light to grow; bone meal speeds them up.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.2.te:
Sugar cane grows next to water, cactus on sand. Melons and pumpkins need a free block beside their stem.
Sugar cane gives paper for books and maps.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.3.te:
- Cows, sheep, goats: wheat
- Pigs: carrots, potatoes, beetroot
- Chickens: seeds
- Horses: golden apples, golden carrots
- Rabbits: carrots, dandelions
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.4.te:
Tame a wolf with bones, a cat with raw cod or salmon, a parrot with seeds.
Wolves fight for you, cats scare creepers and phantoms. Sneak-click a pet to make it sit.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.5.te:
Ride a horse until it stops throwing you off, then saddle it. Horse armor protects it.
Camels carry two riders and eat cactus; donkeys and llamas carry chests.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.6.te:
Bees pollinate crops and fill their hive with honey. Use a glass bottle for honey or shears for honeycomb.
A campfire under the hive keeps the bees calm.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.7.te:
New in 26.x: a dandelion wrapped in gold nuggets. Use it on a baby animal to keep it young; the effect can be undone.
Piglins love it, too.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.8.te:
- Zombies: slow, but in groups
- Skeletons: keep behind cover
- Creepers: explode, back off
- Spiders: climb walls
- Endermen: never look them in the eye
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.9.te:
Stay awake for three nights and phantoms dive at you from the night sky.
Sleeping resets the timer. Their membranes repair elytras and brew slow falling potions.
book.simplebuilding.vanilla_farming.10.t:
- Iron golem: four iron blocks in a T, pumpkin on top
- Snow golem: two snow blocks, pumpkin on top
- Copper golem: a pumpkin on a copper block; it carries items between copper chests
